correctness.rationale: The positive eigenpair of the quotient [[0,ns],[1,s-1]] gives the exact Perron root; s=o(n) gives sp=o(1), nsp→∞ and sigma∼sqrt(c)(ns)^(1/4). Independent clique contributions and an independent conditioning calculation validate the bottleneck variance step: with K~Bin(s,p) open spokes in one clique, its oriented count Z conditional on K is Bin(K(s−K),p), since each edge between an open and a closed spoke appears only once. The independent-copy variance identity and |k(s−k)−l(s−l)|≤(s−1)|k−l| give Var Z_n≤ns(s−1)p²+ns(s−1)²p³. Multiple length-two arrivals cost at most ns*binom(s−1,2)p⁴(1−p) in expectation; every remaining indirect vertex has a simple path entirely inside its own petal, bounded by n(sp)^3/(1−sp). Thus the aggregate mean absolute error is o(s), E Z_n/s→c² for s→∞ and Var Z_n=o(s²) in that regime. E B_n=O(s) handles bounded or irregular sequences at t=0, including s=1 where B_n=0. The binomial CLT and convergence-in-probability shift need no independence between direct and indirect counts; tightness gives divergence in the last regime. The coefficient follows from c²s/sigma∼c^(3/2)(s³/n)^(1/4).
residual_risks: Independent exact rational replay: let d_1=1 and d_k=1−sum_{j=1}^{k−1} binom(k−1,j−1)d_j(1−p)^{j(k−j)}; root-component size k has mass binom(s,k−1)d_k(1−p)^{k(s+1−k)}. Subtract E K=sp from its mean minus one, and compute E Z, Var Z and E B_2 via the binomial law of K, with E[B_2|K]=(s−K)(1−(1−p)^K). Verified the exact moment and analytic bounds for all ten rational test pairs in the source, at s=1 through 5. These tests are finite only. The bundled checker uses s³p⁴ rather than s³p⁴/2 in its error bound and increments a bookkeeping counter; its reported 203236 should not be read as a literal count of independently evaluated assert statements or as a variance check. The proof of the sharper bound does not rely on it.

value.rationale: This addresses a natural fluctuation question left by order-level spectral bounds on a highly irregular family. The exact center at the actual spoke mean matters at the transition, and the theorem distinguishes invisible, finite and overwhelming drift produced by internal clique edges, including a usable mean-shift constant. It is not a claim of a new percolation threshold.
residual_risks: Only the rooted statistic and s=o(n) with fixed c are assessed, not the largest component or a recentered above-window CLT.
